summary: 'Network Egress Resilience' surcharge applied to finalized invoice for private deployment during region failover
description:
Issue summary: Customer FinMate reports an unexpected invoice surcharge line titled 'Network Egress Resilience' on invoice INV-2026-03-09-8765. The charge appears after a cross-region failover from eu-west to us-east during a short private deployment VPN flapping event.

Impact: Finalized invoice shows a one-time surcharge of $2,450 applied to the month; customer believes this is an operational resilience fee mistakenly applied to private VPC traffic during failover. Finance flagged as high-impact for an enterprise customer and withheld autopay.

Environment: Private deployment (VPC) using dedicated private control plane; region primary eu-west with automatic fallback to us-east. Customer reports failover window 2026-03-09T02:17:00Z to 2026-03-09T02:42:00Z.

Steps to reproduce / observed events:
1) Customer ran normal traffic; automated routing detected degraded peering and triggered region fallback to us-east.
2) During fallback, billing tags on postback stream included a transient tag "egress_resilience_charge" emitted by the routing agent.
3) Billing pipeline treated this tag as an auditable surcharge and applied a finalized invoice line.

Observed behavior: One-time surcharge line with description "Network Egress Resilience" and code NER-001 appears on finalized invoice. No prior communication or opt-in for resilience surcharge. Customer expects standard private-deploy billing (no host-level resilience surcharge).

Expected behavior: Resilience or emergency surcharges should only be applied if the customer's contract explicitly includes the add-on or after prior notification/approval. Fallback routing should not auto-emit billable surcharge tags without reconciliation.

Attachments / logs: Invoice PDF (INV-2026-03-09-8765.pdf) uploaded by customer; sample postback snippet quoted in comments; routing-agent logs linked in investigation notes.
investigation_notes:
Initial triage (2026-03-10): Billing ingestion shows a new tag name 'egress_resilience_charge' added to postbacks during region failover. The tag originates from routing-agent v2.7.1 (deployed 2026-03-08) which included an internal telemetry change to tag resilience handoffs for analytics. It was incorrectly mapped in the billing tag-to-rate-table as billable.

Checks performed:
- Cross-referenced postback logs for tenant finmate-001 between 2026-03-09T02:00Z and 2026-03-09T03:00Z (link: logs.prod.redwood/finmate/2026-03-09/failover).
- Reviewed billing mapping table commit (https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing-config/commit/ef12c4) which added mapping 'egress_resilience_charge' -> RATE_SURCHARGE_NER.
- Confirmed customer's contract (SLA Rider v3) does not include NER add-on.
- Reproduced local ingest with synthetic postbacks; charging occurs when mapping present.

Hypothesis: Recent routing-agent release emitted analytics tag that was not intended for billing. Billing-config repo mistakenly treated analytics tags as billable rate IDs during a recent merge.

Action items:
- Block immediate propagation of 'egress_resilience_charge' in billing ingest (hotfix) — ACTION: Billing Ops.
- Issue patch to billing-config to remove mapping and add explicit allowlist for surcharge rate IDs — ACTION: Billing Eng.
- Issue customer-facing provisional credit for the charged amount pending reconciliation — ACTION: Support/Finance.
- Postmortem and controls to prevent analytics->billing mapping drift — ACTION: Reliability + Billing.
